regions.region: page 1 article heading, author block, abstract, DOI, and affiliation
regions.finding: The source title and aggregate palladium-catalysed propargylation claim were verified. No reaction arrow, table row, explicit procedure, or experiment-specific yield appears on this page.

unresolved: The abstract does not define experiment-specific structures, quantities, conditions, or yields.
The article mentions no explicit SI association on this page; workspace SI association remains unestablished.

regions.finding: Three generic prior/developing approaches (ionic coupling, radical coupling, and allylic substitution) are classified as literature examples rather than current experiments; generic R groups and absent yields remain unresolved.

regions.region: page 2 Figure 1b Path 1/Path 2 and current concept
regions.finding: Prior hard/soft-nucleophile palladium paths and the authors' generic eta1-propargylic-palladium concept were classified separately from experiments. A/B/C are mechanistic species, not preparations.

unresolved: Figure 1 contains generic R groups and no experiment-specific scale, time, or yield.
Mechanistic species are proposed and not independently observed.

regions.region: page 3 Table 1 reaction header, alternative products 4aa–7aa, rows 1–14, and footnotes
regions.finding: Fourteen independent optimization runs were retained with row temperature, solvent, ligand/loading, 6 h or 24 h time, crude-1H-NMR 3aa yield, 1a recovery, and entry-8 94% isolated yield. Entries 1–7 also preserve narrative non-observation of expected 5aa/6aa; the header's broader 4aa–7aa non-observation is noted without fabricated row mapping.

regions.region: page 3 Results text and substrate-scope introduction
regions.finding: Narrative statements map to Table 1 and the Table 2 rows on page 4; no duplicate prose-only run was created. The detailed 1.0 mmol 3aa procedure appears on page 6 and merges with the matching Table 2 experiment.

unresolved: Optimization rows omit atmosphere, workup, isolated masses, and most isolated-yield bases.
The Table 1 header shows 4aa–7aa as not observed but does not map that full set row-by-row.

regions.region: page 4 Table 2 header and 30 scope product lines
regions.finding: Thirty independent substrate/nucleophile scope experiments were retained with common or footnote-overridden catalyst/ligand/base, DMSO volume, temperature, times, isolated yields, and product targets. High-loading entries 3ia/3gg/3pi and Cs2CO3/40 °C entries 3ao/3ap include their overrides.

regions.region: page 4 Table 2 3aa ordinary and parenthesized scale-up outcomes
regions.finding: The 1.0 mmol/11 h/89% 3aa experiment is merged with the page-6 detailed synthesis. The parenthesized 10 mmol/17 h/89% repeat is a separate record.

regions.region: page 4 Table 2 3ja footnote and main-text practicality discussion
regions.finding: The 8.4 mmol 1j/22 h/51% 3ja run remains its own experiment. Main text explicitly defers 1j/1k structures to SI, so those structures remain label-only and no SI association is inferred.

regions.region: page 4 Discussion introduction to chiral and control experiments
regions.finding: The prose introduces Figure 2 chirality-transfer runs and Figure 3 controls on page 5; those are linked cross-page rather than duplicated.

unresolved: Most Table 2 rows omit atmosphere, workup, purification, and isolated mass on pages 1–6.
The full main-text structures of 1j and 1k are unavailable; SI association remains unestablished.
Compact scope structures remain unverified machine candidates or label-only.

regions.region: page 5 Figure 2 chirality-transfer reaction header and four product arrows
regions.finding: Four distinct (S)-1g reactions were retained: (S)-3ga 79%, (S)-3gd 84%, (S)-3gg 87% with 7.5/9 mol% catalyst/ligand and 60 h, and (S)-3gj 90%; each reports 97% ee.
One (E)-1q/2j experiment gives beta-elimination product (E)-8 in 89%, recovers 2j in 92% by NMR, and does not form desired 9/10; all outcomes remain product/recovery-targeted.
A separate 1r/2j experiment gives no product 11 after 39 h and reports 94% 1r plus 92% 2j recovery.
The two-inversion/racemization discussion is linked to Figure 4 as a mechanism and does not create preparations of IN-1–IN-4.
The prose introduces five distinct Figure 5 transformations shown on page 6; each arrow is represented separately rather than merged by starting product family.

unresolved: Figure 2 omits DMSO volumes, workups, masses, and ee analytical methods.
Figure 3 omits DMSO volumes/workups and the recovery basis for the 1r control.
Mechanistic intermediates are proposed rather than observed.

regions.finding: The plausible dppf-supported chirality-retention cycle and competing racemization branch were classified as one mechanism record; IN-1–IN-4 are not experiments.

regions.region: page 6 Figure 5 upper tandem reaction to (S)-12
regions.finding: A distinct (S)-3gd/1-iodo-4-nitrobenzene/Pd/Cu reaction affords (S)-12 in 69% and 96% ee; page-7 text supplies necessary detailed context without extending visual coverage.
Two separate thermal cyclizations were retained: 3ja→13ja at 130 °C/18 h/82% and (S)-3ga→(S)-13ga at 130 °C/21 h/91%/97% ee.

regions.region: page 6 Figure 5 lower hydrogenation and semihydrogenation arrows
regions.finding: Two separate (S)-3gj reactions were retained. Full hydrogenation to (S)-14 has an unresolved 92% Figure-5 versus 89% detailed-text yield conflict; Lindlar semihydrogenation gives (S,Z)-15 in 89%/97% ee.

regions.region: page 6 Methods and detailed synthesis of 3aa
regions.finding: Exact K2CO3/Pd(OAc)2/dppf/1a/2a/DMSO charges, nitrogen atmosphere, 30 °C/11 h, TLC, cooling, slow acid quench, extraction/washes/drying, chromatography, and 226.4 mg/89% product enrich the ordinary Table 2 3aa record.

unresolved: Figure 5 (S)-14 yield conflicts with the detailed page-7 text: 92% versus 89%.
Cooling/acid-addition durations in the detailed 3aa procedure are not reported.
Page 7 was used only as text context for Figure 5 and is not claimed as visually covered.
